chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes `ddflow/surfaces/declared/records.py`, but the manifest shows no edit to `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. Since the old file was above `[quality].max_file_bytes` and the tests were green before, it must have had a baseline exemption line. After this split, that baseline line points at a deleted path; running the size/quality baseline check will either fail on the missing baseline entry or leave an orphaned exemption, contrary to the stated requirement to delete the baseline line when splitting an offender.

chunk_findings.detail: The `session adopt-orphans` command is declared with a summary saying it attaches prompts/notes recorded with no session id, but unlike the other executable commands in this tuple it has no `call` (and no payload). Given an operator running `ddflow session adopt-orphans`, the command dispatcher has no callable to perform the backfill; it will either fail because the command has no call or silently do nothing, so orphaned prompts/notes are not attached, contradicting the command’s declared behavior and the split’s no-behaviour-change intent.

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the over-limit module, but the manifest shows no corresponding update to `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. Since the deleted file was recorded as exceeding `[quality].max_file_bytes` and previously passed the size ratchet, it must have a baseline entry; leaving that entry after deleting the file makes the ratchet test fail on the missing path (or leaves a stale allowance for a path that no longer exists), contrary to the required cleanup for this split.

chunk_findings.detail: The old `ddflow/surfaces/declared/records.py` was over the 30000-byte `r-small-files` limit while the suite was green before, so it must have had a baseline entry. The manifest deletes that module and adds the split package, but it never edits `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`; after this change the baseline still names the deleted file/size, so the r-small-files baseline check will fail on the stale entry instead of passing with the line removed as required by the split plan.

chunk_findings.detail: When `ddflow_bug_fixed` is called with `tag=True` (for example `{"id": "bug-1", "tag": true, "add": "foo"}`), the command’s `call` returns the tagging result from `_bug_tag`, but the command still declares `payload=( *BUG_FIXED_FIELDS, "tags", "was", "changed")`. The tagging result is the one used by the separate `bug tag` command (`("id", "tags", "was", "changed")`) and is not expected to contain the fixed-only fields in `BUG_FIXED_FIELDS`. Unlike the adjacent `bug invalid` command, which switches payload based on `_reopening(a)`, this command does not switch payload based on `_tagging(a)`, so the declared output fields do not match the returned data for the tagging path; this can cause missing-key failures or malformed tool output for `bug fixed` used as a tag command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/records/bugs_close.py:bug fixed payload

chunk_findings.detail: The moved `_elsewhere` still treats a command as “elsewhere” only when the raw first word `c[0]` is `cd`/`pushd`. For a linked (non-primary) worktree with `forbidden_commands = ["git status @primary"]`, the command `FOO=bar cd /path/to/primary && git status` is split into commands beginning with `["FOO=bar", "cd", "/path/to/primary"]`; `_head` strips the assignment, but `_elsewhere` never checks the resulting head after assignments. It therefore returns `False`, `check` computes `primary = is_primary(cwd)` as `False`, and the `git status @primary` entry is skipped even though the `cd` can move execution into the primary checkout. This is the same bypass as the previous HIGH finding; the required check is on the command head after leading assignments, not only on `c[0]`.

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the over-limit module `ddflow/services/forbidden.py`, but the manifest contains no modification to `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. Since the old module was explicitly described as exceeding `[quality].max_file_bytes` and the pre-split suite was green, it must have had a baseline exception for that path. Leaving that baseline line in place after deleting the module leaves a stale size-ratchet exception (or silently permits recreating the old path under the old allowance), violating the split plan’s required cleanup.
chunk_findings.title: tests/file_size_baseline.txt

chunk_findings.detail: The facade’s `_SUBMODULE_OF` dictionary does not include `"message": "guard"`, even though the manifest for `ddflow/services/forbidden/guard.py` says that module defines a top-level `message`. Because `_reexport.reexport` is driven only by this dictionary, `from ddflow.services.forbidden import message` or `ddflow.services.forbidden.message` now raises `AttributeError` even though the object exists in `guard.py`, breaking the stated old import path and the docstring’s claim that every name defined by the former single module is re-exported.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden/__init__.py:_SUBMODULE_OF

chunk_findings.detail: `_elsewhere` only treats a pipeline element as “elsewhere” when the literal first token is `cd`/`pushd`, so a leading assignment hides the `cd`. Given `cfg.hooks.forbidden_commands = ["git status @primary"]`, a non-primary `cwd`, no `DDFLOW_HOOKS_ALLOW`, and the command `FOO=bar cd /repo && git status`, `_commands` yields a first element beginning with `FOO=bar`; `_head(c)` would strip the assignment and reveal `cd`, but the `cd`/`pushd` check happens before `_head(c)` is computed. `_elsewhere` returns False, `is_primary(cwd)` is False, and `check` returns `None`, even though the command changes directory and runs `git status` in the primary checkout. The same bypass applies to `FOO=bar pushd /repo && git status`.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier baseline finding still holds: this change deletes the over-limit module `ddflow/services/forbidden.py`, but the manifest contains no modification to `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. Since the old module was explicitly described as over `[quality].max_file_bytes` and the pre-split suite was green, its size-ratchet exception must be recorded in that baseline; after deletion the line still names a path that no longer exists. This violates the split plan’s required cleanup and leaves a stale ratchet entry, which can fail the size-ratchet test or silently permit recreating the deleted path under the old baseline size.

chunk_findings.detail:
Given text such as `echo '<<EOF'
git push
EOF
` (or `echo "<<EOF"
git push
EOF
`), `_strip_heredocs` treats the `<<EOF` inside the quoted argument as a real heredoc redirect: `_HEREDOC` only looks behind for `<`, a digit, or `(`, and its optional quote consumes the opening quote. It then sees the later standalone `EOF` line as the terminator and removes the intervening `git push` line before `_scan`/`_split` ever see it. Consequently `_commands(text)` returns only the `echo` command (with the `<<EOF` argument tokenized) and never yields `git push`, so a forbidden command on that line bypasses the guard.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/forbidden/scan.py:_strip_heredocs

chunk_findings.detail: The new facade-preservation test defines `DEFINED` as “what the single module defined before the split,” but that list omits `message`, which the manifest says `ddflow/services/forbidden/guard.py` defines. Because `message` is not in `DEFINED`, `test_a_name_resolves_from_the_old_path_to_the_object_its_part_defines` never exercises `getattr(FB, "message")`. If the package facade does not re-export `message` (as previously reported for `_SUBMODULE_OF`), `from ddflow.services.forbidden import message` raises `AttributeError`, yet the added split test still passes. The change therefore does not actually verify that the old import path preserves this public name.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_forbidden_split.py:15

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes `ddflow/services/forbidden.py`, which the stated intent says was over `max_file_bytes` (30000). Since the pre-split suite was green, that file must have had a baseline exception; the required cleanup was to delete its line from `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. The manifest contains no change to that file, so the stale baseline entry remains. That leaves a size-ratchet exception pointing at a path that no longer exists and can silently permit recreating the old path under the old baseline size.
